chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, when al-Ḥusayn, ṣalawāt Allāh be upon him, went to al-ʿIrāq, he entrusted Umm Salamah, raḍiya Allāhu ʿanhā, with the books and the bequest. Then when ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام returned, she handed them over to him.

key_terms.أُمَّ سَلَمَةَ: Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها, the custodian of the entrusted items
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنَ: Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, the one who entrusted the sacred deposit
key_terms.الْعِرَاقِ: Iraq, the region to which Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام traveled
key_terms.الْكُتُبَ: the books, referring to preserved written materials of authority
key_terms.عَلِيُّ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ: Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, to whom the deposit was delivered

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith indicate the transfer of the Imam’s books and bequest after Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration reports that Imam al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام entrusted the books and the waṣiyyah to Umm Salamah رضي الله عنها before departing to al-ʿIrāq. After the return of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, she delivered them to him, indicating continuity of the entrusted authority and transmission within the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abu Bakr Al Hazramy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup>, when he<sup>asws</sup> went to Al-Iraq, deposited with Umm Salma<sup>as</sup>, the Book and the bequest. So when Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> returned (to Al-Medina), she<sup>as</sup> handed it over to him<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Sayf ibn ‘Amira from abu Bakr al-Hadrami from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.
